bug_semantics: ExpressAuthorizationMiddleware.getMatchedAction() and middleware() fed req.originalUrl (path plus query string) into path-to-regexp matchers built from Cedar SimpleRest httpPathTemplate annotations, while Express itself routes on the path only. With overlapping templates such as GET /users (restrictive) and GET /users/{id} (permissive), a request like GET /users/?x=1 was authorized as the parameterized action (id captured as the query tail) but executed by Express as the collection handler, bypassing the stricter Cedar policy. CWE-436/CWE-863; GHSA/CVE still published, not withdrawn.
flaw_origin: The originalUrl-based matcher was first written when src/index.ts was added in a8cd22f862f6e4a80d187f24062219e02271a3d1 (v 0.1, package 0.1.0). shouldBeSkipped already split on '?' as a safety strip, but getMatchedAction used the raw originalUrl for Cedar action selection. Those two assignments were unchanged through v0.2.0 and were replaced with req.path in 3d23c4a23d5537f605d242f6095b22c488df74b8, released as v0.3.0.
